The book ends here; the program does not. A few directions to take it.

Build cells of your own

Every part in Part III works in an empty sandbox the way it does on the template, and the program’s test suite builds a scrap cell from the parts list in an empty floor every release: a Raised Conveyor with a Bottle Feeder, a Broken-bottle Eye, a pivot gate over a Grinder, a Box Conveyor with a Box Feeder and Box Photoeye, a second gate over a Divert Conveyor, and six rungs — a run bit, the belts, a gate on its own photoeye, the box conveyor on LS, the shredder on an empty box. It runs. Start there.

Real hardware

Bridge & Tools runs the TcpBridge program on your PC that connects the page to the outside: a TCP socket a vision system or a test bench talks to (the TCP Client Socket part), and EtherNet/IP devices. Communications → Start Bridge, then the socket part’s settings. Help → Bridge & Tools covers it.

The bench

The Card Sort Cell (chapter 65) is a model of a real bench fixture, and Help → Bench Files has the printable parts and the camera cards, so the same program can be tried against a real camera on a real bench through the bridge.

Studio 5000

Export L5X and import the file into Studio 5000: the tags, aliases and routines come across, and the program that ran the simulated line is the program you would download to a CompactLogix driving the real one — the I/O addresses are already in the right shape. Going the other way, Import L5X brings a real project’s routines in to run against a sandbox machine you lay out to match.
